calibration_add.note: The AI is read-only, so a tool that writes is not offered.

calibration_measure_sensor_noise.note: With save on, it writes a measured gain and read noise into the camera profile in the configuration file. The AI is read-only.

calibration_query.note: Built 2026-10-05. Calibration counts, or how a target's light frames match the darks. refresh reloads the index into memory and writes nothing.

calibration_refresh.note: The AI is read-only, so a tool that writes is not offered.

calibration_save.note: Writes the calibration index. The AI is read-only.

jobs_query.note: Built 2026-10-03. Reads jobs, log tails, stored results and data lineage from the logs database, opened read-only. A job stuck at 'started' after the app stopped still shows as active.

processing_acquire_analysis_slot.note: Internal concurrency lock exposed by reflection.

processing_acquire_stacking_slot.note: Internal concurrency lock exposed by reflection.

processing_discard_previous_stack.note: The AI is read-only, so a tool that writes is not offered.

processing_measure_odd_even_difference_n.note: Stacks two halves of a target's frames into the target's _subsets folder (about one library stack's time in all), subtracts them, and writes the noise of the difference into the quality database. The halves are deleted afterwards, and the library stack, its previews and its records are never changed. The AI is read-only, so it reads the stored numbers with quality_query instead.

processing_measure_night_contributions.note: Stacks some of a target's frames into the target's _subsets folder (never over the library stack, its previews or its records) and writes the noise of each result into the quality database. It costs one stack for each subset, so it takes minutes. The AI is read-only, so it reads the stored numbers with quality_query instead.

processing_measure_noise_growth.note: Stacks some of a target's frames into the target's _subsets folder (never over the library stack, its previews or its records) and writes the noise of each result into the quality database. It costs one stack for each subset, so it takes minutes. The AI is read-only, so it reads the stored numbers with quality_query instead.

processing_process_target.note: The AI is read-only, so a tool that writes is not offered.

processing_record_frame_measurements.note: Measures a target's light frames and writes the numbers into the quality database, and stamps each measured frame on the target record. It never changes a frame file. The AI is read-only, so it reads the stored numbers with quality_query instead.

processing_remake_preview.note: Built 2026-10-04 from gap report #1. Makes a target's preview picture again from its existing stack, without restacking. denoise, denoise_strength and star_toning apply to that run only and never reach the configuration. The old pictures are copied into _previous_preview first and put back if the run fails. The stack file is never written. Writes only the preview JPEG, the processed FITS and the target's processed-image pointer.

processing_restore_excluded_frames.note: The AI is read-only, so a tool that writes is not offered.

processing_run_spectroscopy_by_session.note: Needs Python objects, so it cannot be called through MCP. Consider making it a stage of pipeline_run.

processing_stack.note: Built 2026-10-04 at the user's request: the AI may stack a target the way the app's Stack button does, choosing imaging or spectral frames, a filter and a file or time range. plan_only lists the frames without stacking. It runs the app's own stage: sets aside bad frames into _excluded (never deletes), keeps one previous stack, and saves the target. Since 2026-10-05 it is ProcessingPipelines.stack, which also takes the exact frames to stack.

processing_stack_subset.note: Stacks some of a target's frames into the target's _subsets folder (never over the library stack, its previews or its records) and writes the noise of each result into the quality database. It costs one stack for each subset, so it takes minutes. The AI is read-only, so it reads the stored numbers with quality_query instead.

processing_stack_summary.note: Built 2026-10-04. One short answer for a target's stack: frames stacked and skipped, rejected fraction, star width against the inputs, flags and each exposure group. Reads the saved summary.

processing_swap_with_previous_stack.note: The AI is read-only, so a tool that writes is not offered.

quality_calibration_identities.note: Built 2026-10-25. Reads which flat, bias and dark masters, optic, camera, Siril version and stacking algorithm version each library stacking run used, by run id or target, so two runs confounded by a calibration change can be told apart. Writes nothing and creates no table.

quality_capture_settings.note: Built 2026-10-24. Reads the camera, telescope, filter, exposure, gain setting, offset and binning that stored quality measurements point at, by capture setting id. Writes nothing and creates no table.

quality_check_spectral_frames.note: Built 2026-10-04. Measures raw spectrum frames: zero-order position, tilt, width, peaks, saturated patches along the spectrum, a predicted peak at another exposure, and a summary by exposure and by pier side. Nothing is saved.

quality_flag_value_outliers.note: Arithmetic on numbers the caller passes in. The user does not want it.

quality_measure_frames.note: Built 2026-10-03. Statistics on raw frames. Nothing is saved.

quality_measure_stack.note: Built 2026-10-05. Measures a stack (star width, rejected share, registration) and compares it with the previous stack or another stack file. Saves nothing.

quality_metrics.note: Built 2026-10-21. Lists the declared quality metrics (or one, given its name, or those of one checkpoint). The default detail is a short summary (unit, checkpoint, levels, purpose); detail=full adds the meaning, which way is better and how it is estimated. Fixed text, nothing is read from disk.

quality_query.note: Built 2026-10-21. Reads the quality measurements that earlier runs stored (the latest for each subject and metric, or every row). Writes nothing and creates no table.

quality_resolve_rows.note: Built 2026-10-25. Turns stored quality row ids into the frame or stack file each row is about, with a plain reason when a picture cannot be found, and lists the ids no row has. Reads only.

quality_set_aside_frames.note: Built 2026-10-24. Lists the frames lying in a target's _excluded folders with the kind and reason, and says whether the reason came from a stored quality row, the folder's manifest file, or nothing but the folder. Moves nothing and writes nothing.

star_analyze_periodicity.note: Writes the result into the live star catalog. Needs a save=false option.

star_create.note: The AI is read-only, so a tool that writes is not offered.

star_detect_point_sources.note: Needs a NumPy array, which MCP cannot send. Take a frame path.

star_find_or_create_by_position.note: The AI is read-only, so a tool that writes is not offered.

star_get.note: Reads one star's full record by id. Writes nothing.

star_plate_solve.note: Returns an astropy WCS, which MCP cannot send. Return the solved center and pixel scale.

star_query.note: Built 2026-10-03. Library star lookup with hard caps on rows, region size and full records.

star_tune_spectroscopy_calibration.note: Rewrites the live configuration file through update_config. Needs an apply=false mode that only returns the fitted values.

star_update.note: The AI is read-only, so a tool that writes is not offered.

target_add.note: The AI is read-only, so a tool that writes is not offered.

target_create.note: The AI is read-only, so a tool that writes is not offered.

target_get_frame.note: Returns the path of one frame, found by ISO, exposure and index.

target_imaged_field_centers.note: Built 2026-10-04. The distinct sky positions imaged, read from FITS headers (about 35 s on this library), so it runs as a background job.

target_query.note: Built 2026-10-04. Targets as short rows or one grouped record, the cameras used, or each target's frames per camera; replaces target_get and target_list.

target_read_saved.note: Returns the whole target record, frames and all, which overflows the reply. Use target_query.

target_reindex_frames.note: Writes the frame records. A dry_run mode that only reports what would change would let an AI use it.

target_save.note: Writes the database. The AI is read-only.

visualization_get_last_captured_image.interim_block: Returns the picture as base64 text, which the 40,000 character reply limit cuts in half. Use visualization_render_fits with a path, which returns a real image.
visualization_get_last_captured_image.note: Returns base64 text that the reply limit cuts in half. Make it return an image, or fold it into visualization_render_fits with a latest option.

visualization_plot.note: Built 2026-10-05. Draws one chart of a target or a star; the registry sends it as a PNG image. Saves nothing.

visualization_render_fits.note: Built 2026-10-03. Returns a real image of a frame, with a stretch and an optional zoom. Saves nothing.
